This confirms it: `system.properties` (loaded by `SystemProperties`) never contains an `exist.home` key — it only has build-time metadata (vendor, version, build, git-commit). So `SystemProperties.getInstance().getSystemProperty("exist.home", "unknown")` will always fall back to `"unknown"`, whereas `exist.home` is actually a JVM system property set by the launcher (`System.getProperty("exist.home")`).

The bug-fixing commit reverts this specific line back to `System.getProperty("exist.home", "unknown")`. Tracing history with `git log -S` on that exact call shows only two commits ever introduced/touched that literal string: the fix itself (1856857af) and an older commit c342cbc05.

content.text:
In commit `c342cbc05` (2011-04-19), the author introduced the `SystemProperties` class (which loads a static, build-time `org/exist/system.properties` resource) and, while refactoring the version/build logging in `JettyStart.java`, mistakenly changed the "eXist Home" line from `System.getProperty("exist.home")` to `SystemProperties.getInstance().getSystemProperty("exist.home", "unknown")`. This is a copy-paste error — `exist.home` is a runtime JVM system property, not a build-time constant in `system.properties` (which only contains `vendor`, `product-version`, `product-build`, `git-commit`, etc.), so the log line has always silently printed `"unknown"` since that commit. The 2016 fix (1856857af) reverts exactly this line back to `System.getProperty(...)`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: c342cbc05e44f776f0055b8182abbf4550a6c459

## Reasoning
(1) I diffed the fix and saw it simply swapped `SystemProperties.getInstance().getSystemProperty("exist.home", "unknown")` back to `System.getProperty("exist.home", "unknown")`. I used `git log -S'SystemProperties.getInstance().getSystemProperty("exist.home"'` on `JettyStart.java` to find every commit that added/removed that exact call — it returned only the fix commit and one older commit, `c342cbc05`.

(2) In `c342cbc05`, while adding the new `SystemProperties` class and refactoring the startup logging (replacing manual `Properties` loading with calls to `SystemProperties.getInstance()`), the author changed three genuinely build-time properties (`product-version`, `product-build`, `svn-revision`) correctly, but also changed the "eXist Home" line the same way — even though `exist.home` is not a build-time property, it's a JVM system property set at runtime by the launch scripts.

(3) I confirmed `SystemProperties.java` only loads `org/exist/system.properties`, and that resource file contains only `vendor`, `vendor-url`, `product-name`, `product-version`, `product-semver`, `product-build`, `git-commit` — no `exist.home` key. So since commit `c342cbc05`, the "eXist Home" log line has always fallen back to the default `"unknown"` string, which is the bug the 2016 commit fixes.

I'm confident in this identification since the fix is a direct textual revert of the exact line introduced in `c342cbc05`, and the surrounding code/resource files corroborate why that call could never have worked correctly.
